title: BLUE & WHITE PLATE & 4 BISQUE ...
reason: Four antique looking continental bisque figures (two with script titles) plus a large blue onion dish; unmarked so value rests on age and maker; likely $80-200 (my estimate).
findings: A large blue and white onion pattern (Zwiebelmuster style) dish with a scalloped rim and a hand-written number ending '142' on the rim edge (inventory style, not a maker mark). The base is not photographed, so Meissen or other factory marks cannot be checked; the pattern was made by Meissen and many other factories, so do not assume Meissen. Four pastel bisque figures, unmarked except for hand-lettered script on two bases: a bearded sailor waving a cloth with a spar under his arm, base script reads 'Distress' (fairly clear); a bearded fisherman with an anchor on his shirt holding a rope or net, base has a short script title (illegible); a boy in a feathered hat playing a guitar or mandolin; and a girl in a bonnet and striped apron. The style looks late 19th to early 20th century continental (probably German) bisque. No impressed numbers or factory marks seen (bases not photographed from underneath).
condition: Figures look intact in the photos with bright colour; no breaks seen, though small losses to fingers or props are not ruled out; the plate shows no cracks in the photos.
rescore_note: Four pastel bisque figures (probably German, c.1900, unmarked, one titled Distress) plus a large blue onion dish that looks like a standard factory print and is unlikely to be Meissen with the base unseen; decorative but a soft market, my estimate about $90 to $150 (no live comps).
